persona: Jordan Lee is 38 years old and grew up in suburban Evanston, Illinois, just outside Chicago, where their parents ran a small specialty food shop that sourced local producers and curated seasonal menus for neighborhood cafes. They attended the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, where they double-majored in Industrial Engineering and Marketing, minored in data analytics, and spent a summer interning at a regional CPG manufacturer that used early predictive models for inventory optimization. After college, Jordan spent four years as a business development manager at a cloud infrastructure firm serving mid-market retailers, where they led go-to-market strategy for a migration platform that helped grocery chains digitize back-office workflows. They closed their first $2M deal at 31 by partnering with a Chief Merchandising Officer to replace legacy spreadsheets with a cloud-based demand forecasting system powered by machine learning—later expanded to include dynamic pricing and shelf-space allocation using GenAI. Now based in Chicago, Jordan lives in a modest two-bedroom apartment near the Gold Coast with their partner and two young kids, who often hear them sketching customer journey maps on napkins during dinner. They rise early to run five days a week, usually walking the dog around the lakefront before checking pipeline metrics, and they keep a small notebook in their bag where they jot down phrases customers use unprompted—like “We need to stop guessing inventory” or “Can we test what if?” They speak to CMOs and CTOs with calm precision, often starting meetings by asking, “What part of your week feels most repetitive or risky?” rather than pitching features. They’ve built a habit of sending one short, value-focused follow-up email after every meeting—no agenda, no jargon—just a one-sentence recap of what the customer said and one practical next step. They enjoy cooking Sunday lunches for friends, trying out new Chicago bakeries, and occasionally volunteering at a local food co-op to help organize donations. Jordan doesn’t use titles in conversation; they say “we” when talking about customer teams. They’re observant, quietly confident, and genuinely curious—not flashy, but consistently reliable. They remember small details: the name of a buyer’s dog, the pain point from last quarter’s rollout, the fact that a client prefers email over calls after 4 p.m. They don’t chase quotas; they track them naturally because they focus first on solving real bottlenecks. Their energy is steady, not performative—present, patient, and precise. They believe cloud adoption should feel like removing friction, not adding complexity, and they show that belief every time they translate “supply chain optimization” into “fewer stockouts and less overtime for planning teams.”

persona: Lena Park is 28 years old and grew up in the modest, tree‑lined neighborhood of Eastwood in Portland, Oregon, where she spent most weekends at the local thrift store digging through racks for anything that felt fresh and personal. She graduated high school in 2016 and spent a year at Portland Community College studying fashion merchandising before transferring to the University of Oregon, where she earned a bachelor’s degree in fashion design in 2019. After graduation she worked part‑time as a visual merchandiser at a boutique clothing shop downtown while freelancing on small style consultations for friends; those early gigs taught her how to talk about fabrics, fit, and emerging trends in everyday language. In the past year she moved back to Portland to take a full‑time role as a Sales Advisor at H&M, living in a modest two‑bedroom apartment a few blocks from the store, where she bikes to work most days and spends evenings curating playlists for friends or trying out new coffee spots. Lena describes herself as warm, observant, and quick to ask questions—she notices the small details a customer mentions about comfort or style and follows up with a relevant suggestion. She enjoys chatting with shoppers about what they’re looking for, shares easy care tips from the in‑store app, and takes a few minutes after each shift to tidy the fitting rooms and restock shelves so the floor stays inviting. Curious by nature, she follows a handful of local designers and sustainable fashion blogs, reads the weekly H&M trend bulletin, and updates her mental “style cheat sheet” each morning. She values collaboration, often looping teammates into quick “what worked today?” huddles and sharing a recent customer compliment over coffee. Outside of work she volunteers once a month with a neighborhood clothing swap, helps friends plan capsule wardrobes, and spends weekends hiking nearby trails with her golden retriever, Scout. Lena’s everyday rhythm reflects her belief that good service feels personal—she greets each visitor by name when she can, offers a brief story behind a piece (“this print was inspired by coastal murals from last summer”), and gently nudges them toward the loyalty app without making it feel salesy. Her practical lifestyle—biking, modest housing, and a habit of quick clean‑up after shifts—mirrors the efficient, tidy store environment she helps maintain, while her genuine enthusiasm for fashion, curiosity about trends, and collaborative spirit align perfectly with H&M’s values.

persona: Jamal Reyes is 32 years old and grew up in Silver Spring, Maryland, where he spent his teenage years sketching wine labels on notebook margins after school, inspired by the bottles his mother brought home from Total Wine stores on weekend visits. He studied Graphic Design at Maryland Institute College of Art, graduating in 2019 with a thesis focused on visual storytelling for consumer goods—designing mockups of fictional boutique spirits paired with seasonal menus, emphasizing texture, label hierarchy, and emotional resonance. Since then, he’s worked full-time in Total Wine’s in-house creative studio in Bethesda for the past three years, first as a junior designer on holiday campaign rollouts, then as a digital designer handling web banners, app mockups, and social assets for wine club promotions. Jamal spends his mornings brewing cold-brew coffee on his kitchen counter while reviewing Figma prototypes on his MacBook, often pausing to adjust type scales or test color contrast against WCAG standards—he once spent 45 minutes tweaking a wine label’s serif weight because the cap height felt “off” when viewed on a phone screen at arm’s length. He cycles to work most days, wears minimalist navy workwear (no logos), and keeps a small shelf in his bedroom with printed proofs, a few actual wine labels he designed for internal mockups, and a notebook where he jots down phrases like “clarity over cleverness” after seeing a customer hesitate on a product page. He’s collaborative but precise—during cross-functional reviews with merchandising, he’ll quietly ask, “Who’s clicking this on a 320px screen?” before suggesting a layout tweak. He knows the difference between “looks nice” and “drives engagement,” which is why he once redesigned a summer cocktail banner using a tighter grid, simpler iconography, and alt-text descriptions for screen readers—resulting in a 22% increase in click-throughs. He occasionally stops by Total Wine stores on weekends not to shop, but to observe how customers interact with shelf signage and digital kiosks, noting where labels feel crowded or where lighting makes colors appear dull. Jamal values quiet consistency—he doesn’t chase trends; he tests them against usability and accessibility first. He’s thoughtful, observant, and quietly confident, the kind of designer who listens closely during handoffs, asks clarifying questions, and follows up with a single, polished asset that meets the brief without over-explaining. He’s also the person who remembers to add “pet-friendly” signage to event graphics when a local dog park partners with Total Wine for a tasting—small details that feel genuinely human. He lives in a modest but well-organized two-bedroom apartment near downtown Bethesda, where his space includes a small desk by the window for sketching, a shelf of actual wine bottles (mostly local Maryland producers), and a framed print of his first professional campaign mockup—still slightly imperfect, but proudly signed.

persona: Jordan Reyes is 42 years old and grew up in Aurora, Colorado, just a few blocks from the old train depot where their parents ran a modest taco cart at weekend farmers’ markets. They attended Aurora Central High School, then earned a Bachelor of Science in Culinary Arts from Johnson & Wales University in Denver, where they double‑majored in food science and nutrition. After graduating in 2013, Jordan spent five years as sous‑chef and then executive chef at a boutique hotel in downtown Denver, overseeing breakfast buffets, weekend brunch menus, and private event prep while consistently keeping food cost variance under 3 %. In 2018 they led the kitchen transformation at a historic resort near Rocky Mountain National Park, introducing seasonal wild‑foraged ingredients and instituting a waste‑audit program that cut landfill waste by 40 %. Today Jordan works full‑time as the Executive Chef at Stonebridge Hotel in Aurora, reporting to the General Manager and supervising a team of twelve culinary staff. They rise early to walk the kitchen floor, tasting sauces before service, checking mise en place, and chatting with line cooks about how the day’s prep feels. Jordan’s kitchen is organized like a well‑kept notebook—color‑coded prep stations, labeled freezer bins, and a small whiteboard that lists daily cost targets. Off‑hours they jog along Cherry Creek Trail, tend a small herb garden on their balcony, and spend Sundays teaching free cooking demos for local high‑school students, emphasizing simple techniques and reducing waste. Their demeanor is calm but energized; they listen first, ask precise questions (“How does the texture feel after the second sear?”), give concise feedback (“Try a lighter hand on the salt; the broth needs balance”), and celebrate small wins (“Great job keeping the garnish fresh all service”). Friends describe Jordan as approachable, detail‑oriented, and quietly confident—someone who can handle the heat of a busy dinner rush while still pausing to check that every staff member’s schedule is clear and comfortable. Their lived experience in both urban hotel kitchens and mountain‑focused hospitality gives them a practical sense of sourcing locally, respecting health codes, and turning seasonal ingredients into memorable guest experiences.

The Marketing Manager will be responsible for executing lead generation, digital marketing, social media, SEO, content marketing, and campaign initiatives that support pipeline growth for Globalli's global payroll and HCM platform.

This role is designed for a hands-on marketing professional who has experience supporting or leading lead generation initiatives and is ready to take broader ownership of revenue-focused marketing programs in a fast-paced SaaS environment.

The role is focused on execution, optimization, and measurable performance outcomes, working closely with Sales and Leadership to support lead generation and customer acquisition.

What You'll Do

Lead Generation & Pipeline Support

  • Execute marketing campaigns to drive qualified leads and support sales pipeline growth
  • Support inbound and outbound marketing initiatives across digital and social channels
  • Collaborate with Sales to align campaigns with target customer segments and revenue priorities
  • Monitor and optimize campaign performance based on conversion and engagement metrics

Social Media & Content Marketing

  • Own execution of social media strategy and day-to-day management across LinkedIn and other relevant platforms
  • Manage execution of content marketing initiatives across LinkedIn, email, and web channels
  • Support development and distribution of thought leadership, product messaging, and customer stories
  • Maintain a content and social calendar, ensuring consistent execution and posting cadence
  • Support brand awareness through consistent digital and social presence across channels

SEO & Website Optimization

  • Execute SEO initiatives to improve organic visibility and website traffic
  • Identify keyword opportunities and support content optimization efforts
  • Monitor website performance and recommend improvements to increase engagement and conversions

Marketing Systems & Reporting

  • Use HubSpot and other marketing tools to execute and track campaigns
  • Maintain accurate marketing data and campaign tracking
  • Monitor key performance metrics including lead volume, traffic, social engagement, and conversion rates
  • Provide regular reporting on campaign performance and insights

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Work closely with Sales, Product, Customer Success, and Leadership teams
  • Support go-to-market initiatives including product updates and campaign launches
  • Contribute to improving marketing effectiveness through feedback and insights

What You'll Bring

Experience

  • 4–7+ years of experience in Marketing, Lead Generation, Social Media, or Digital Marketing
  • Experience in B2B SaaS strongly preferred
  • Exposure to lead generation, social media management, or revenue-focused marketing programs
  • Experience working with Sales teams or revenue-driven environments

Skills

  • Strong understanding of digital marketing, lead generation, social media strategy, and campaign execution
  • Experience managing social media platforms (especially LinkedIn), email marketing, and content distribution
  • Strong writing and communication skills
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment
  • Analytical mindset with ability to interpret marketing performance data

Technical

  • Experience with HubSpot or similar CRM/marketing automation tools
  • Familiarity with SEO tools and website analytics (e.g., Google Analytics)
  • Comfortable working with marketing funnel metrics and reporting dashboards

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in HR tech, payroll, PEO, or fintech SaaS environments
  • Experience in high-growth or early-stage startup environments
  • Exposure to account-based marketing (ABM) or lifecycle marketing
  • Experience supporting or coordinating freelancers, agencies, or interns (not required)

Growing up in a family that valued hands-on craftsmanship and emotional resilience, Evelyn developed a keen understanding of the importance of restoring what was lost. She graduated with a degree in Environmental Science from the University of Texas at Austin, where her coursework cultivated her passion for environmental preservation and restoration techniques. Her studies were complemented by internships with local environmental non-profits, which laid the groundwork for her future career in restoration.

Today, Evelyn balances her time between her home in Austin, where she resides in a sunlit apartment filled with reclaimed furniture and art pieces she's helped restore, and the occasional travels required by her job. Her current lifestyle is marked by a strong commitment to physical fitness and mental clarity, as she knows the demands of her job require both mental acuity and physical strength. Evelyn is an advocate for sustainable practices and enjoys spending her weekends exploring Texas' natural landscapes with her trusty dog, a rescue labrador named Rusty.

With a professional demeanor that exudes urgency and a positive attitude, Evelyn's leadership skills shine brightly. Her strong work ethic and customer-centric approach have made her a go-to figure for clients dealing with the aftermath of disaster. She thrives in multitasking environments and takes pride in her ability to plan and manage multiple restoration projects simultaneously. Evelyn's interpersonal communication skills are honed through her role as a point of contact for homeowners and insurers, ensuring them not only the technical expertise but also the emotional support they need during challenging times.

Evelyn holds a forklift certification, a driver's license, and possesses a comprehensive understanding of customer service principles. Her background in restoration, coupled with her willingness to travel up to 75% for training or project support, makes her an ideal fit for the Blue Kangaroo Packoutz team. Evelyn's detailed orientation and organizational skills allow her to efficiently manage inventories and ensure the safe transport and cleaning of client contents. Her life's trajectory has prepared her not just for the technical demands of the job, but also for the emotional labor of consoling clients during their most vulnerable moments. Evelyn Carter is the embodiment of resilience and restoration, ready to bring Blue Kangaroo PACKOUTZ's vision to life with dedication and care.

Company Overview:

Blue Kangaroo Packoutz is the trusted name for comprehensive contents, furniture, art, and document restoration services. We offer comprehensive contents cleaning and restoration solutions to help homeowners, property owners, businesses, and institutions restore what they value most. Clients seek out Blue Kangaroo PACKOUTZ after fire, water, mold, or other damage—it’s a very sensitive situation they’re facing, so we work hard to make the restoration process seamless and stress-free.

Benefits/Perks:

  • Career Advancement Opportunities
  • Paid Training (must be willing to travel for initial training)
  • Active Work Environment

Job Summary:

This position is responsible to both supervise and provide operational support in packout and remediation efforts for homeowner contents. Main functions will include overseeing and performing tasks related to contents packing, moving, and cleaning; deodorizing; manipulation; and storage. Pay will be dependent upon experience with potential for bonus opportunities.

Responsibilities:

  • Oversee the inventory, packout, cleaning, vaulting, wrapping, staging, and pack back of contents
  • Point of contact communicating with homeowners and insurers, while reporting to General Managers
  • Responsible for the safety program and training new hires
  • Perform Dry and Wet mitigation/pre-cleaning using accepted procedures
  • Manipulate contents at the client site to allow for the remediation crew to perform required tasks

  • Correctly wrap and package contents to prevent damage during transport
  • Accurately load and unload contents on and off the truck

  • Eligible to operate a motor vehicle per Blue Kangaroo PACKOUTZ’s vehicle policy
  • Forklift certification or ability to become certified

  • Strong customer orientation with excellent interpersonal communication skills
  • Ability to lead and multitask in a fast-paced environment
  • Comprehensive understanding of customer service principles and practices Physical Requirements

  • Access and mobility in tight spaces
